content.title: Ryan Day reveals format for Ohio State football spring game
content.text: Updated April 13, 2026, 3:19 p.m. ETOhio State is planning for its spring football game at noon April 18 to include tackling for most of the intrasquad scrimmage. “We’re excited about that,” Buckeyes coach Ryan Day said. “It’s a great opportunity, because of our numbers, to let guys get out there and play in front of a good crowd.”Day said the Buckeyes would reserve one or two drives for “thud” tempo, but otherwise be in full contact as they end spring practice at Ohio Stadium. The scrimmage will feature the offense against the defense rather than divide the roster into separate teams.The Buckeyes used a similar format for last year’s spring game, which replaced a previously scheduled spring showcase.The length of their 2024 national championship run prompted Day to consider a more scaled-down version before opting for the more competitive format.“What you realize is these guys coming out of high school really need to play,” Day said. “They haven’t played at this level, and it’s a big jump for all of them. There are guys, however, that have played 500 or a thousand or more snaps. Those guys really don't need that as much, but there's a lot of guys on the team they do.”The elimination of the spring transfer portal window, condensing the roster movement to a period of weeks in January, also left the Buckeyes with more players to use as part of their scrimmage. In previous years, a handful of transfers would not enroll until May or June.“You pretty much know what your team is at this point,” Day said. “It allows you enough players to get out there and actually scrimmage, and we need to do that. So that's what we're going to do, but we'll also be smart and make sure we're not putting guys who have played a whole bunch of football out there and risk any type of injury.”Joey Kaufman covers Ohio State football for The Columbus Dispatch.
